name: Sam Sip
description: Sam Sip (Pa-Som Sip) is a draw-and-discard game from Thailand and Burma. Players draw from the stock or the previous player's discard, then discard one card. The aim is to be the first to hold three pairs: two cards totalling 10 (Ace=1), two 10s, or two equal picture cards (J, Q, K). Wild cards (jokers and cards matching the turned-up rank) can substitute for any card. The Thai name means "mixing tens".

rules.objective: Be the first player to hold six cards forming three pairs: two cards that add up to 10 (Ace=1), two 10s, or two equal picture cards (J, Q, K). Wild cards (jokers and cards matching the turned-up rank) substitute for any card. Special wins: three Aces plus any three other cards, or six cards of the same suit.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal: Five cards each, counter-clockwise; one card turned up (wild indicator). Dealer stacks remainder as stock.
2. Play: Dealer draws one from stock (has six cards), discards one face up in front of the player to his right. Each turn: take either the top card of the stock or the top discard in front of you (the card just discarded by the previous player), then discard one face up in front of the next player. Only the most recent discard in front of you is available.
3. Winning: As soon as a player has six cards in hand forming three valid pairs, they win the deal. Pairs are: two cards totalling 10, two 10s, two Jacks, two Queens, or two Kings. Wild cards (three jokers plus three cards of the turned-up rank) can complete any pair.
keyRules: Draw one each turn from stock or the single discard in front of you (from the previous player).
Discard one face up in front of the next player after drawing.
Pairs: two cards summing to 10 (Ace=1), or two 10s/J/Q/K. Wilds substitute for any card.
First to hold three pairs in hand wins the deal.

scoring.description: Each deal is won by the first player to hold three pairs (two cards totalling 10, two 10s, or two equal picture cards). Stakes are paid per deal; in match play, more deals won is better.
scoring.winCondition: Win the deal by being the first to hold six cards forming three valid pairs. In match play, the player or side that wins the most deals wins.
